answer.rationale: Constraints dominate: 14 days to expiry, line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, and one decision slot. Switching primary supply (memory_c2) is the only lever that plausibly delivers the full 18% on unit cost, so it is the memory most worth verifying "onboarding was quick" against the original record \u2014 quick onboarding under slack capacity is not evidence of safe onboarding at 94% utilization with a hard expiry, and if that record turns out to be a different part class or a low-volume ramp, the switch is disqualified. memory_c4 is the second verification because negotiate_terms is my intended action and I am relying on its claim that benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms; I need to see whether the recovered margin was a few points or anywhere near 18%, since that determines whether negotiation alone can meet the finance mandate. Current intent is negotiate_terms combined with a multi-year structure per memory_c6, because it captures cost without migration work and preserves the delivery continuity in memory_c1 \u2014 it is the only option that moves TCO without adding delivery risk during a no-buffer window. Risks I am carrying forward rather than resolving: negotiation may close only part of the 18% gap, and hard price pressure can silently erode service scope or quality even when the contract language holds constant, so any concession must be checked against scope rather than headline unit cost. Multi-year lock-in also forecloses the switch option and leaves the single point of failure that memory_c3 says was worth removing; add_second_source stays queued as the next review's decision. defer_decision (memory_c5) does not transfer \u2014 that was a non-critical service on month-to-month terms, not a primary supply contract with no auto-renew and no line buffer. If verification undercuts memory_c4's magnitude and confirms memory_c2's onboarding claim under comparable load, I would shift toward a staged switch with the incumbent extended as bridge cover rather than a clean vendor change.
